Your farm question
Crop health
Potato
Pest / feeding damage
Holes or feeding damage: what to do now

First check whether the damage is on leaves, stems, or the harvested part. Holes alone do not identify the pest.

Steps you can take now
Inspect both leaf surfaces, rolled leaves and nearby stems for larvae, eggs, droppings or webbing.
On a few plants, collect clearly identified leaf-eating caterpillars using gloves or tongs. Avoid handling hairy or unfamiliar insects.
Compare new damage on the same marked plants. Do not spray an unknown insect or repeat pesticide mixtures just because holes are present.

If young plants are being cut, new damage is spreading quickly, or tubers/fruit are affected, arrange a local inspection promptly.

To narrow it down: Where are the holes? Are insects visible, and is the damage spreading?

Why these steps? Sources
On potato leaves, many tiny shot-like holes with small jumping beetles can suggest flea-beetle feeding. Larger chewed areas need a check for caterpillars or other feeders. Inspect before naming or treating the insect.
